mistakes.note: Narration says Nell 'had laid him out herself' and she swears to the neck mark from it, as Dacre (M42), Harriet (M27) and Price (M68) also take as done, but the page followed her through all of Monday and the night and she never went near the body; a round-20 Choice even offers 'what the laying-out showed'. The body's own clues are never looked at.

The cottage is said to have been forced and every board prised up 'in the night' by lantern (M66, M70, M82), yet Kit slept there with the latch chained (M40) and Nell and Price stood at its door at eight (M42); nobody sees the splintered latch until half past ten. The Plot Thread has Grout searching till near dawn with the boy in the house.
The tide is going out in the early afternoon (M2) after a dawn low tide and is 'out' at M10, then has 'turned since morning' and is coming in at M21 and high by evening.
The bed's patchwork is turned down 'where Price had pulled it back to look', two Messages after Kit said Price never went past the table.
Price talks of the knee Nell set right; the World Bible says she set his broken wrist.

The Anchor, on the quay beside the cottage until now, drifts 'up the hill' and 'ten minutes off': Kit and the runner are sent up the hill to Dacre, and Nell climbs past the chandler's and the grocer to reach it (M82).
Price says the boy beat him to the cottage and took the scrap to the coroner, though he left the Anchor before Kit was sent, has only just arrived and was told by no one.

Dacre says he will 'ride at one' though noon struck at M80 and he had already put the cart off an hour (M82), and tells Thorne that Mrs Ashby has the evidence in her keeping after sealing the hair in his own envelope and carrying it (M84, M86).
Grout's eyes go over 'the four of them' when only Nell, Dacre and Thorne are on the path.
Dacre, who has never been inside the crypt, tells Nell to mind the ninth step because it talks; the line belongs to Thorne.
Harriet gives up the secret that would ruin her (the marriage, the cottage, her suspicion) in her first breath, before Nell has said or shown anything.
The Choice picked asks Kit what he 'meant to tell me last night', when Kit left nothing unsaid at M40; the reply quietly drops the premise.
A Choice offers going to reach the slate before Price and keep the scrap, three rounds after Nell sent Kit to fetch it.

Looks hold invented and passing things: Dacre's newspaper and watch in his palm, the grocer's flour, apron and pipe-packing (round 23), Grout's chisel through his belt and 'in his forties' against thirty years as sexton (round 42).
Price's looks are rewritten only to add 'and his hat', and his portrait is redrawn with a peaked cap for no change on the page.
What the chandler's man saw and heard at the cottage is recorded as the Grocer juror's knowledge (again in round 31); the page keeps them two men (M82).
Harriet is recorded as told that Price warned Kit 'before and after the inquest'; both warnings came before it.
A Known fact, and Price's knowledge, say Harriet accused Price of ringing the chapel bell; she said only that it rang and that it is the sexton's to ring.
The redrawn portrait wraps both her forearms and hands in white bandage (the knee bandage misplaced), and the bandaged arms follow her through every scene picture from M36 on.

Kit is drawn inside the shop pushing at the door, in a khaki jacket with a medal, where the page has him outside knocking on the glass in a pea jacket; his jacket stays khaki in the scenes against the navy of his portrait.
The 1894 Revenue cutter is drawn as a modern motor vessel, and Nell is missing from the porch; M96 has motor cars on the quay and puts Dacre outside with the lantern.
At the crypt door Nell is hatless and another woman's face, Dacre is a dark-haired younger man, and Grout wears a clerical collar and holds a cleaver rather than a chisel.
He has a moustache and tattooed hands where the page gives thick kinked black hair on the backs of his hands, the clue the hair rests on.

choices.reason: Three real paths nearly every round and picks bend what follows (the cord spent at the inquest, Kit sent for the scrap), with a few built on a false or stale premise.

surprise.reason: The world moves out of sight (Price reaching Kit first, the searched cottage, Price at the box, Grout on the path), though the three behind it are signposted and the search's timing is not fair in hindsight.

threads.reason: The inquest thread reaches its ending on time and bent to Nell's evidence, and the others move each few rounds, but Grout's night search ignores the boy asleep in the house.

characters.reason: Kit, Harriet, Price, Dacre and Grout each want something and sound like themselves; Harriet tells all at once and Price and Dacre each speak from what they were never told.

continuity.reason: A search told as done in the night in a cottage where Kit slept, a laying-out that never happened, and a run of small slips (tide, knee, the Anchor's place, the cart's hour, four on the path).

pacing.reason: Every reply adds a fact or a turn, the inquest is brisk and the cottage standoff and the walk to the crypt run long but keep tightening.

prose.reason: Vivid period voice with real similes, marked by tics: the half-turned cup, the watch, 'earned its keep', 'mouth went dry' twice, and a few garbled lines.

pictures.reason: Most scenes show the moment and the right people, but Nell's arms are bandaged in every picture from M36, Kit's jacket changes colour, the cutter is a modern ship and the crypt-door picture is off-model.

secrets.reason: The narration, Choices and Journal give nothing away; Kit still keeps the lantern and Thorne's and Price's parts reach Nell only as hints on the page.

agency.reason: Each move is carried out as given with little added, the laying-out claimed for her aside.

stakes.reason: Eleven Checks; failures cost for good (the scrap crumbled, the button lost to the sea, the scrap's hiding place blurted, Price turned against her), though Dacre and Thorne yield to pressing without a roll.

state.reason: Rewrite, Regenerate, Edit and World Change all leave clean state, but several records are wrong or padded: looks, the grocer's knowledge, a Known fact about the bell, a Plot Thread now.

mystery.reason: Fair clues placed before they matter (the missing cord, the burnt scrap, the snug meeting, the hair and chisel, the vicar's glance), looks answered honestly with failed rolls giving less, and no confession; held back by the body never being examined on the page and a break-in whose timing cannot fit.
